item.title: Putting it to a vote: Hacked Fridges and Data Center Backlash
item.description:
What's on the ballot from the economy to foie gras...
Good morning and welcome home to Karl Bushby. The UK native finally made it back to his mother’s house in England yesterday, after completing a 28-year, 31,000-mile walk home from Punta Arenas, Chile. Bushby’s long walk, which started on Nov. 1, 1998, spanned four continents and 30 countries and included swimming across the English Channel. Upon arrival, his mother asked him, “Where have you been?” This is a good story to tell your own mom when she asks why you haven’t bought your ticket home for the holidays yet.

item.title: Endurance Brew: The Booming Industry of Extreme Suffering
item.description:
Taking things to extremes is having a moment...
Good morning. It’s Marathon Day in NYC today, but here in the cozy confines of the Brew, we’re taking it up a notch by running you through the business behind events that are even more extreme than marathons (without having to leave bed). We’re talkin’ the rise of Ironman competitions and “darecations,” frigid swims through ice water and foot races through the Sahara Desert, plus a whole lot more. Welcome to...Endurance Brew.
